question: Does mechanical equivalence of walker-stand/walk/run justify changing only the task argument of TD-MPC2 latent dynamics while keeping the encoder, policy, reward and Q task fixed to the victim?

decision.physical_forecast_invariance_claim: No-Go under the proposed raw-latent comparison: the source does not establish a task-invariant latent coordinate or physical-readout contract.
decision.scope: This excludes the proposed interpretation and unqualified test, not the possibility of a correctly specified task-routing integrity study or a future independently validated physical-readout/alignment diagnostic.
decision.not_established: Source inspection does not prove the checkpoint actually uses different coordinates or measure any task-swap harm. It proves that cross-task identity of its latent predictions is not imposed by these interfaces or losses.

code_facts.fact: Multitask state encoding appends the task embedding to the observation before the encoder; the encoder input dimension explicitly includes task_dim. Thus E_t(o) may depend on t even at the same physical observation.
The latent dynamics appends the task embedding to z and concatenates the action before predicting another latent. Its output is not an explicit physical state.

Training computes next_z=encode(obs[1:], task), starts its rollout with encode(obs[0], task), and fits next(z,a,task) to these same-task encoded successors. No equality between encodings or forecasts for two different tasks appears in this consistency objective.

Reward and Q targets are also task dependent. TD targets use the same-task next latent, policy, task discount, target Q and observed reward. Predicted reward/Q losses use the same task on the imagined latents.

Native planning encodes observations with the victim task and passes one task consistently through policy-prior rollout, dynamics, reward, discount and terminal policy/Q. Changing only next(task) breaks this consistent task context.

A global override of model.next also changes the policy-prior trajectory generator before value scoring. Therefore keeping the policy network weights and task argument fixed does not guarantee the prior candidate actions remain unchanged.

The inspected native architecture exposes encoder, dynamics, reward, optional termination, policy and Q modules; it contains no latent-to-physical-state/observation decoder. The inspected training loss consists of consistency, reward, optional termination and value terms, without a physical reconstruction term.
code_facts.search_scope: Bounded source search of vendor/tdmpc2/tdmpc2 and src/wm_security/tdmpc_native.py for decoder/decode/reconstruct; not a claim that no external diagnostic readout exists anywhere.

mechanical_equivalence_scope.source_basis: The locally installed dm_control source creates stand/walk/run from the same walker.xml, Physics class, control timestep and PlanarWalker class. The move_speed differs and is consumed by the reward. Observation construction is shared.
mechanical_equivalence_scope.conditional_physical_contract: Given identical complete simulator state and parameters, wrapper/control timing, physical action sequence and relevant randomness, changing only the walker reward preference should not alter the physical trajectory. Task reward itself may legitimately change.
mechanical_equivalence_scope.not_verified: No environment was constructed, replayed or reset; the installed source was read without importing it. No runtime equivalence or checkpoint availability of every listed task ID was tested here.
mechanical_equivalence_scope.does_not_imply: This physical statement does not entail E_v(o)=E_d(o), F_v(E_v(o),a)=F_d(E_d(o),a), or F_d(E_v(o),a)=F_v(E_v(o),a) as raw tensors.

representation_contract.trained_relation: F_t(E_t(o), a) approximately matches E_t(o_next), with the same t on both sides.
representation_contract.proposed_mixed_relation: F_d(E_v(o), a) has no demonstrated contract to output E_v(o_next). Feeding it into victim-task reward, policy or Q heads adds a potential representation-compatibility confound.
representation_contract.why_shared_weights_are_insufficient: Shared weights, latent dimensions and SimNorm output constraints do not enforce task-independent semantic coordinates or interchangeable readouts.
representation_contract.why_fixing_head_task_is_insufficient: The scalar task label at a downstream victim head can remain fixed while the meaning or distribution of its latent input changes. A lower return would not by itself establish corruption of a task-independent physical prediction.
representation_contract.not_a_measured_ood_claim: The source permits this mismatch; whether the particular trained checkpoint aligns or ignores task embeddings is unmeasured. Do not assert empirical OOD magnitude or inevitable failure.

common_requirements: Fix the complete physical root, victim objective and utility, physical candidate action sequences, control timing and relevant RNG; obtain independent real successor states/observations.
Define the output being compared in common physical units or in a separately validated common latent coordinate system before inspecting task-swap outcomes.
Keep prediction fidelity, native scalar reward/Q scoring and true selected-action utility separate. Equal tensor shapes and raw latent L2 changes are not physical prediction errors.

If a fixed-candidate ranking test is intended, avoid inadvertently changing the native policy-prior candidate generator through a global next override; any added scoring adapter or frozen candidate bank must be identified explicitly.

physical_readout_option.criterion: Use a validated readout R_t from each task-consistent latent to the same physical quantity y, and compare R_v(F_v(E_v(o),a)) and R_d(F_d(E_d(o),a)) against the independently measured same physical y_next. Readout accuracy and uncertainty must be established on held-out physical states before interpreting forecast differences.
physical_readout_option.availability: No such native readout was found in the inspected architecture. No decoder, mapping, weights or validation scores are invented or supplied by this review.
physical_readout_option.limit: A newly trained diagnostic readout is an added component, may omit relevant state dimensions, and does not automatically create a drop-in native victim reward/Q interface.

aligned_coordinate_option.criterion: If a mapping A_d_to_v exists, independently establish A_d_to_v(E_d(o)) approximately equals E_v(o) on held-out states and assess A_d_to_v(F_d(E_d(o),a)) against E_v(o_next) on held-out real transitions and relevant rollout lengths. Only then compare predictions in victim coordinates or feed the converted latent to victim heads.
aligned_coordinate_option.availability: No validated A_d_to_v is known from the inspected source. Do not assume an identity, linear, orthogonal or invertible map.
aligned_coordinate_option.limit: An aligned donor rollout must start with donor-consistent encoding and maintain donor coordinates internally; mapping only its output does not repair the original unvalidated mixed input F_d(E_v(o),a). Any added conversion changes the tested system and must be disclosed.

valid_possible_test_criterion.minimum_action_now: Record the source-level contract failure and do not execute the proposed next-only task swap as a physical-invariance or Goal-Swap attack test. A valid readout/alignment is a prerequisite to that interpretation, not a fabricated result or an instruction to train one now.

claim_limits: No attack success, forecast error, action change or utility result was measured.
No claim of a new security mechanism or numeric novelty score.

This conclusion concerns the proposed physical-prediction interpretation; a transparently defined mixed-task interface fault could be studied for a different question, without calling raw latent divergence a physics violation.
No blocked WorldAgen/GammaWorld branch was read or revived.
